alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism likely driving weight gain and symptoms
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L with low free T4 despite levothyroxine 50 mcg, plus tiredness, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflex relaxation — classic overt hypothyroidism. She reports often forgetting the thyroid tablet, making under-treatment and poor adherence the most likely explanation. Weight gain of 9 kg over the past year is more consistent with untreated hypothyroidism than with DTG, which guidelines note may not be causally associated with weight gain. Switching DTG for weight gain would be a misattribution while the thyroid is uncontrolled. Fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L is not diabetic range, further arguing against DTG-driven metabolic dysfunction.

evidence.recommended_action: Do not switch DTG for weight gain at this visit. Address levothyroxine adherence, recheck TSH after adherence improvement, and consider dose titration per endocrine guidance.

alerts.title: Planned DTG switch conflicts with guideline evidence on weight gain
alerts.message: Guidelines state the association between integrase inhibitors and weight gain now appears not to be causal, possibly reflecting less metabolic toxicity than older regimens. The clinician plans to switch from DTG because of weight gain, but this patient has a clear alternative cause: overt hypothyroidism with TSH 12.4 and low free T4, plus poor levothyroxine adherence. Viral load is suppressed on the current regimen. Switching away from DTG risks losing a well-tolerated, effective first-line regimen without addressing the actual cause of weight gain.

evidence.recommended_action: Defer DTG switch. Correct hypothyroidism and reassess weight after thyroid control before considering any ART change.

alerts.title: Hyperglycaemia risk factors warrant glucose screening on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend checking glucose in patients starting or transitioning to DTG who have two or more hyperglycaemia risk factors (age ≥30, BMI ≥25, hypertension, family history of diabetes). This patient has at least two risk factors: age 45 and BMI 33. Today's fasting glucose of 5.6 mmol/L is reassuring and below diabetic range, but guidelines support glucose monitoring in this context. No further action beyond awareness of the result is needed today given the normal value.

evidence.recommended_action: Note fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L is normal. Continue periodic glucose monitoring given BMI 33 and age per guideline risk-factor screening.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring interval approaching on DTG regimen
alerts.message: Guidelines specify viral load checks every 6 months for patients on two NRTIs plus DTG, reducible to 12-monthly only if VL <50 copies/mL for over a year with reliable adherence. Last viral load was <50 copies/mL on 2025-11-10, 106 days ago. The next 6-monthly viral load is due around May 2026. No viral load was ordered today, which is acceptable timing-wise but should be scheduled.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule next viral load for approximately May 2026 per 6-monthly DTG monitoring schedule.

alerts.title: Amitriptyline effects may compound hypothyroid symptoms
alerts.message: Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly can cause weight gain, constipation, and sedation, which overlap with and may compound the patient's hypothyroid symptoms of weight gain, constipation, and tiredness. This contributes to the clinical picture but is a secondary factor compared to the overtly elevated TSH of 12.4 with low free T4. Distinguishing contributors matters for treatment: correcting hypothyroidism should be prioritised, and amitriptyline review may be considered if symptoms persist after thyroid correction.

evidence.recommended_action: Review amitriptyline necessity and dose with mental health team after thyroid correction; consider alternatives if weight and sedation remain problematic.
